messages.subject: tRophic position with one isotope only
messages.subject_clean: tRophic position with one isotope only
messages.body_plain:
Hola Claudio

I forward (here) the raw question from a colleague not (yet) on this group: Is it possible (and pertinent?) to apply trophic position on a dataset of one isotope only?

If I have to answer I would say possible but with a lot of uncertainties. But I think you would have a more detailed answer!

All the best

Pierre

messages.subject: Re: [tRophicPosition-support] tRophic position with one isotope only
messages.subject_clean: [tRophicPosition-support] tRophic position with one isotope only
messages.body_plain:
Hola Pierre

Yes, it is possible (and pertinent). When you are calculating a one baseline model you are actually using only one isotope (just nitrogen). If you have one isotope it only prevents to make a nice biplot (because we use both N & C in the plot), but otherwise, it can be done.

I'm not sure if the package will work if you are actually using only one isotope. But if not, just create/simulate the other isotope and use a one baseline model and it should work fine.

Cheers

Claudio

messages.subject: Difficultly loading multiple consumers
messages.body_plain:
Good afternoon Dr. Quezada-Romegialli,
  I am trying to build trophic position models for a large community of fish with two baselines using version 0.7.7 in R 3.6.1 via RStudio 1.2.1335.

I am closely following the Bilagay example and have tried to format my data the same way. However, the extractIsotopeData function creates a nested list with empty entries for the isotope data, but does not generate any errors. I've tried grouping the data a number of ways and have had no luck. If I run your example code exactly as written, I can recreate your Bilagay analyses easily, so I don't think the problem is in my version of the package. I am also able to use generateTPData to manually create an isotopeData object for various consumers. I have a large number to generate, however, and it's impractical to do them all manually.

I've attached a screenshot of some of my data, the code I have run, and what the nested list looks like. I would really appreciate any help you could offer with getting the code to work. Do you see any errors in my code or data structure?

Thank you!
Hannah

--
Hannah M Carroll

PhD Candidate, Iowa State University
Department of Ecology, Evolution, and Organismal Biology

--------------------------------
Office: 357 Bessey Hall
Mailbox: 251 Bessey Hall

messages.body_plain:

Is there any solution to that issue?

Cheers,
Gabriel C. Cardozo-Ferreira, PhD.
